title: New Alphabet
description: A word drawn in an original raster alphabet: only horizontal and vertical strokes and 45-degree corners, every vertex sitting on a visible dot grid. Drag across the field and the raster coarsens or refines; each letter rebuilds itself stroke by stroke, its strokes sliding along the grid to their new dots, so the word stays legible from a five-dot screen to a fine one. Type to set a new word.
intent: After Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet (1967), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Alphabet: accept the screen's raster completely and make the letterforms a system of it. Here the raster is the variable, and the system has to hold at every pitch.
